posts.text:
75 by 19 by 90 mm, 1 solid, 23 faces, 66 edges, kernel check passed.

That is a wall-mounted phone holder, built from one sentence on CAD Forge, live now at three.ws/cad. Not a mesh guess: a parametric build123d program the OpenCascade kernel has accepted, with every key size as a slider and STEP, STL, GLB, a drawing sheet and the Python program itself to download.

When the kernel rejects a program, its real error (kind, message, failing line) goes back to the writer, which rewrites it, up to three times. Nothing is shown until the kernel has accepted it. Moving a slider rebuilds the same program with only that value changed, on the kernel, with no model involved. Standard parts come from bd_warehouse: involute spur gears, ISO threads, nuts, cap screws, washers and ball bearings. The Python runs anywhere after pip install build123d bd_warehouse.
